title: Synthetic Load Testing & Observability Lab — Workshop Guide
content:
Purpose:
This hands-on lab walks SEs and customer engineers through building a reproducible synthetic load test for Redwood Inference endpoints, wiring up observability (Prometheus + Grafana), and iterating on performance knobs (batching, KV cache, model variants, autoscale). The goal is to create a short, repeatable experiment you can run during a customer POC to demonstrate throughput, latency SLOs, and the cost/quality tradeoffs of different serving configurations.

Intended audience:
- Solutions engineers running POCs with customers who want to verify latency/cost at scale
- Customer infra/ML engineers evaluating Redwood Dedicated or Private deployments

Estimated time: 2.5–3 hours (can be split across sessions)

Learning objectives:
- Deploy a temporary test endpoint with a controlled model variant and autoscale profile
- Generate realistic synthetic traffic (token-level mixes) and measure p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU util, and token throughput
- Configure Prometheus metrics collection and import a Grafana dashboard for inference KPIs
- Experiment with batching, prefix caching, and quantized model variants to observe latency vs. cost tradeoffs
- Produce a short artifact (CSV + dashboard snapshot) to attach to a customer POC report

Prerequisites:
- Redwood org account with the ability to create temporary endpoints (RBAC: se-deploy role)
- Kubernetes cluster or Redwood Dedicated test pool pre-configured (instructions in linked GitHub repo)
- Prometheus and Grafana installed in the same cluster or accessible to the test control plane
- Locust or Vegeta installed on a load generator host (small VM)
- Example prompt set (provided in repo) that approximates customer traffic: short-chat, long-document, and reranking calls

Quick environment checklist (commands you can run on laptop):
- Verify access: redwood auth whoami
- View clusters: redwood infra clusters list --org <org-id>
- Clone lab repo: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/lab-loadgen.git

Step 0 — Prep a test model and endpoint
1) Choose model variant: pick a baseline FP16 and a quantized-8 variant if available (we will compare both).
2) Create endpoint (example using redwood CLI):

# create temporary endpoint with explicit autoscale + batching config
redwood endpoints create --name se-loadtest-01 --model redwood-7b-quant8 --min-instances 1 --max-instances 4 --batching "enabled=true,max_tokens=2048,max_batch=64" --kv-cache enabled

3) Record the endpoint id from the CLI output. You will use it in the load generator.

Step 1 — Baseline profile collection (no load)
- After endpoint is READY, call a simple prompt 10x to ensure warmup and KV cache population: use the small prompt set in repo/examples/warmup.txt
- Collect baseline metrics for 1 minute: record GPU memory usage, queue length (serving_runtime.queue_length), and token/sec.

Prometheus example queries to run now (PromQL):
- 95th latency (server-side): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le))
- Tokens per second: sum(rate(redwood_inference_tokens_emitted_total[1m]))
- KV cache hit rate: sum(rate(redwood_inference_kv_cache_hits_total[1m])) / sum(rate(redwood_inference_kv_cache_requests_total[1m]))
- GPU utilization (node exporter metric): avg(instance:node_gpu_utilization:ratio) by (instance)

Step 2 — Synthetic load profiles
We include three profiles in the repo: chatty-short, long-context, and reranker-batch. Each profile contains JSON payloads and target token distributions. Start with chatty-short (higher RPS, short token lengths) to stress throughput.

Example Vegeta workload file (repo/examples/chatty-targets.txt):
GET http://<load-generator-host>/invoke
Header: Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>
Body: {"endpoint_id":"<ENDPOINT_ID>", "prompt":"Summarize this sentence: The quick brown fox…", "max_tokens":64}

Local wrapper to transform vegeta hits into Redwood API calls (bash):
#!/usr/bin/env bash
API_KEY=$1
ENDPOINT=$2
while IFS= read -r line; do
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/endpoints/$ENDPOINT/invoke" \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d "$line" >/dev/null
done < chatty-targets.txt

Vegetal run (example):
vegeta attack -duration=3m -rate=120 -targets=repo/examples/chatty-targets.txt | vegeta report

Step 3 — Run experiments and collect traces
For each experiment run the following matrix:
- Model variant: fp16 vs quant8
- Batching: max_batch 16 vs 64
- KV cache: enabled vs disabled
- Autoscale profile: conservative (min=1,max=2) vs aggressive (min=1,max=6)

Run each config for 3 minutes; collect Prometheus metrics and a full export of traces for the same window. Use a naming convention for artifacts: <model>-batch<N>-cache<on|off>-scale<max>.csv

Sample Python snippet to call endpoint and log latency percentiles (repo/tools/benchmark.py):
import requests, time, statistics
API = "https://api.redwood.example/v1/endpoints/{}/invoke"
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer {}"}

def run_one(endpoint_id, api_key, prompt):
    timings = []
    for i in range(100):
        payload = {"prompt": prompt, "max_tokens": 64}
        start = time.time()
        r = requests.post(API.format(endpoint_id), headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}"}, json=payload)
        timings.append((time.time() - start) * 1000)
    return statistics.quantiles(timings, n=100)
Note: the python above is intentionally small — it’s used only to sanity-check p50/p95 locally before the vegeta runs.

Step 4 — Dashboard & alerting setup
- Import the included Grafana JSON dashboard (repo/dashboards/inference-kpis.json). It contains panels for:
  - p50/p95/p99 server latency (split by model variant)
  - tokens/sec and requests/sec
  - GPU utilization and memory
  - Batch size distribution and queue length
  - KV cache hit rate
- Suggested alert rules:
  - p95 latency > 800ms for 2m -> alert on call
  - GPU util > 85% for 5m -> scale or throttle
  - KV cache hit rate < 30% -> consider warmup or longer prefix caching

Troubleshooting checklist (common POC issues)
- High queue length but low GPU util -> check batching config and batch timeouts; increase max_batch or lower batch_timeout_ms.
- Stable high latency after enabling quant8 variant -> verify kernel/quantization fallback in runtime logs (redwood-runtime logs show quant-fallback warnings).
- Unpredictable p99 spikes -> confirm request size distribution; look for long-context requests that force cache misses and recompute attention for every token.
- Endpoint returning 503s under load -> inspect autoscale events and pod restart reasons (oom, preemption). If preemption visible, schedule on dedicated non-preemptible pool.

Dos and Don’ts when running customer demos
- DO keep the load generator and the endpoint in the same region to avoid network noise in latency tests.
- DO share raw CSV + dashboard snapshot with customers for reproducibility.
- DON’T run long-context profiles with extreme RPS without a checked autoscale policy — you will burn commit quickly.

Artifact checklist to produce at end of lab
- CSV of raw latency samples for every experiment run
- Grafana dashboard snapshot (PNG) and dashboard JSON export
- Short notes summarizing which config hit target SLOs and which reduced cost per token the most
- Follow-up recommendation: suggested Dedicated pool size and autoscale bounds for customer production traffic (one-page)

Extensions / advanced topics (optional follow-ups)
- Add network degradation schedules using tc/netem to measure the impact of tail latency for real-world WAN conditions.
- Integrate real user prompt traces (synthesized) to create more realistic token distributions.
- Use a tracer (OpenTelemetry) to correlate request traces to GPU-side kernel timings for deeper root cause analysis.

Appendix: quick commands and useful endpoints
- List endpoints: redwood endpoints list --org <org-id>
- Get endpoint metrics snapshot: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API" https://api.redwood.example/v1/endpoints/<id>/metrics?window=1m
- Download dashboard JSON: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API" https://api.redwood.example/v1/admin/dashboards/inference-kpis > inference-kpis.json

Repo and support
- Workshop repo (code, targets, dashboards): https://github.com/redwood-inference/lab-loadgen
- Contact for help during POC: se-support@redwood.example (on-call weekdays 09:00-17:00 PT)

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add a short slide deck summarizing the experiment results for customer handoff.
- Add an automated notebook that runs the full matrix and uploads CSVs + dashboard snapshot to shared drive.
- Validate quant8 variant on small A100 pool for consistent baseline.
